key_insight: Extending characteristic mapping to dissipative equations preserves its fine-scale resolution strategy while enabling applications to Navier–Stokes flows.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support efficient, high-resolution simulation of turbulent flows across a broad range of Reynolds numbers.
method: Lift scalar evolution equations to paths in a diffeomorphism group, interpreted through optimal transport.
Represent flow maps as compositions of spatial interpolants and evolve them with semi-Lagrangian characteristic mapping.
Use semidirect product time stepping with an exponential integrator for the map’s log-Jacobian.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-order accuracy and tests on canonical nonlinear dissipative equations, but provides no quantitative error or runtime results.
watch_item: Performance and robustness across all Reynolds numbers remain promising rather than established by the abstract’s reported evidence.
paper_title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
